name: Lysergic acid hydroxyethylamide
summary: Lysergic acid hydroxyethylamide (LSH or LAH), also known as lysergic acid N-(α-hydroxyethyl)amide or as lysergic acid methyl carbinolamide, is a lysergamide alkaloid related to the psychedelic drug lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD).

pharmacology.text: The pharmacology of LSH has been very limitedly studied.

uses.text: According to Albert Hofmann, Alexander Shulgin, and other researchers, LSH might be a psychedelic drug and might contribute to or be substantially responsible for the hallucinogenic effects of morning glory seeds. Relatedly, per Shulgin in his 1997 book TiHKAL (Tryptamines I Have Known and Loved), both ergine (lysergic acid amide; LSA) and isoergine (iso-LSA) are "probably correctly dismissed" as not contributing to the effects of morning glory seeds.
